metadata.case_name: WONG YAN LAM v. LAM WING KEI; WONG YAN LAM v. INTERCONTINENTAL HIRE CARS LIMITED & LEE FU YIU (consolidated)

plaintiff.occupation_before: Clerk at Gigamind International Education Development Co. Ltd. (a primary school)
plaintiff.occupation_after: Employed by father-in-law in an engineering firm (from March 2009)
plaintiff.education_level: Diploma of Business; undertaking Bachelor of Business Administration (University of Canberra, distance learning)

injuries.description: multiple contusions to her neck, right shoulder and low back
injuries.body_part: neck, right shoulder and low back
source: the plaintiff sustained multiple contusions to her neck, right shoulder and low back,
she suffered a sprained neck and experienced right shoulder pain.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of cervical spine

source: She was diagnosed as suffering from post traumatic stress disorder

manifestations.description: Lost consciousness for a while after the first accident
Severe headaches (constant headache; severe headaches especially after midnight with resultant loss of sleep)
Neck pain and right shoulder pain
Limited movement in the neck and shoulders
Weakness of the right upper limb and pain on lifting things
Paraesthesia and weakness of the ulnar thenar finger
Vomits froth every two or three days; blurred vision; afraid of bright light requiring constant wearing of sunglasses
Tenderness over posterior aspect and slight stiffness (neck); tenderness of back muscles
Fear of travelling; anxiety when travelling on buses
Inability to write for more than about 10 minutes at a time

treatments_received: Ambulance transport to Caritas Medical Centre
Referral to Orthopaedic and Physiotherapy departments
Private orthopaedic consultations (Dr Ko Wing Man)
MRI examinations of cervical and lumbar spine and brain
Admission for investigation on three occasions (details not specified)
treatments_future: Continued psychological treatment for one year (as suggested by psychiatrists)

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Can no longer enjoy her hobbies and sporting activities such as badminton

losses.category: Loss of ability to volunteer or engage in community service
losses.description: Can no longer continue the voluntary work she enjoyed

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: Fear of travelling and anxiety when travelling on buses

losses.category: Loss of ability to pursue education
losses.description: Had to discontinue studying for a BBA degree; inability to write for more than a few minutes prevented her from taking the last examination
She was diagnosed as suffering from post traumatic stress disorder
